vectors.name: non-canonical-base64url
vectors.why: the last character of the signature segment carries bits no byte uses, so sixteen strings decode to the same 64 bytes; a token that can be rewritten without invalidating it cannot key a one-time-use set

vectors.name: duplicate-header-member
vectors.why: RFC 8259 §4 leaves duplicate members undefined and JSON.parse keeps the last, so this header is EdDSA to one reader and "none" to another

vectors.name: duplicate-payload-member
vectors.why: the same scan on the payload, which a port that only checked the header would let through: two `sub` claims is two answers to "who"

vectors.name: crit-present
vectors.why: `crit` names extensions a verifier must understand; this one implements none, so RFC 7515 §4.1.11 says refuse rather than guess

vectors.name: typ-not-string
vectors.why: RFC 7515 §4.1.9 makes `typ` a media type; `typ: 5` hands every caller that compares it a value its own type says cannot be there

vectors.name: cty-not-string
vectors.why: the same rule for `cty` (RFC 7515 §4.1.10)

vectors.name: alg-none
vectors.why: `alg` is only ever compared to the KEY's algorithm, so "none" is a mismatch and never an invitation to skip the signature check

vectors.name: alg-not-the-keys
vectors.why: the same comparison with a real algorithm: an ES256 header over the Ed25519 key is refused before any signature is checked

vectors.name: unknown-kid
vectors.why: the header names a key this verifier does not hold, which is a verdict of its own and not a bad signature

vectors.name: iat-after-exp
vectors.why: a token that expired before it was issued: no clock makes both claims true, so it is the issuer's bug and not an expiry

vectors.name: non-finite-claim
vectors.why: `1e999` parses to Infinity; treating a present-but-unusable `exp` as "no expiry given" turns a typo into an immortal token

vectors.name: not-yet-valid
vectors.why: `nbf` an hour ahead, well beyond the default 30 seconds of skew

vectors.name: too-old
vectors.why: a token that granted itself a longer life than the caller allows. Only reachable under `maxAgeSec`, which is why the vector carries its own options

vectors.name: no-expiry
vectors.why: under `maxAgeSec` a missing `exp` leaves the lifetime uncomputable, so it is a refusal and not an exemption

vectors.name: rs256-valid
vectors.why: the anchor for RSA keys, which reach a verifier through a JWK Set and never the `kid:key` string

vectors.name: rs256-expired
vectors.why: the same clock rules on RSA as on the curves

vectors.name: rs256-bad-signature
vectors.why: one flipped bit in a signature that is otherwise this key's

vectors.name: rs256-header-on-ed25519-key
vectors.why: an RS256 header naming the Ed25519 key: the key decides the algorithm, so this is refused before any signature is checked

vectors.name: ed25519-header-on-rsa-key
vectors.why: the other direction: an RSA key verifies RS256 and nothing else

vectors.name: rs256-short-signature
vectors.why: a valid signature with its leading zero byte stripped: the same integer, one byte short of the modulus. A signature must be exactly the modulus length, or one token has two encodings

vectors.name: audience-wrong
vectors.why: `aud` is compared exactly: a value the expected one is a prefix of is a different audience

vectors.name: audience-missing
vectors.why: a caller that requires an audience is not satisfied by a token that names none

vectors.name: audience-in-array
vectors.why: RFC 7519 §4.1.3 lets `aud` be an array; one member matching is enough, and the verdict names which

vectors.name: issuer-wrong
vectors.why: the same rule for `iss`

vectors.name: issuer-missing
vectors.why: a missing `iss` is not an exemption from `issuer`

vectors.name: issued-too-long-ago
vectors.why: still inside its own lifetime, but issued earlier than the caller accepts: `issuedWithinSec` bounds the issue date, not the expiry

vectors.name: cross-purpose
vectors.why: a verifier holding one purpose's keys does not hold another's, so a token of the other purpose names a key it does not have

vectors.name: cross-purpose-same-key
vectors.why: if one key did serve two purposes, `aud` still keeps their tokens apart

vectors.name: audience-prefix-ok
vectors.why: the anchor: the prefix, then a remainder that matches `rest` in full. The verdict carries the whole value, so the caller reads the remainder from it

vectors.name: audience-prefix-other-path
vectors.why: a well-formed remainder after a different path is a different audience

vectors.name: audience-prefix-empty-rest
vectors.why: the prefix alone, under a `rest` that accepts the empty string: an empty remainder is refused whatever `rest` says

vectors.name: audience-prefix-rest-mismatch
vectors.why: a remainder of the wrong shape — base64 with `+`, `/` and padding where hex is expected

vectors.name: audience-prefix-extra-path
vectors.why: a matching value followed by more path: `rest` must match the whole remainder, which is what its anchors are for

vectors.name: audience-prefix-missing
vectors.why: no `aud` is not an exemption under a prefix either

jwks.name: jwks-one-of-each
jwks.why: one key of each kind the verifier reads

jwks.name: jwks-unknown-kty
jwks.why: an unknown `kty` and an unknown curve are skipped, not refused: an issuer adding a key of a new kind must not stop verification

jwks.name: jwks-use-enc
jwks.why: a key published for encryption verifies nothing

jwks.name: jwks-unsupported-alg
jwks.why: an `alg` this verifier does not implement — RS384 — is skipped

jwks.name: jwks-weak-rsa
jwks.why: a 1024-bit modulus, under the 2048 bits RFC 7518 §3.3 requires

jwks.name: jwks-non-canonical-n
jwks.why: `n` respelled in its unused low bits: the same bytes under another string

jwks.name: jwks-missing-kid
jwks.why: a key the verifier reads, with no kid to select it by

jwks.name: jwks-duplicate-kid
jwks.why: two keys under one kid: which one verifies is a coin toss

jwks.name: jwks-nothing-usable
jwks.why: every key skipped leaves a set that verifies nothing

jwks.name: jwks-alg-contradicts-key
jwks.why: an RSA key labelled ES256 says two things about it

jwks.name: jwks-private-member
jwks.why: a published set carrying private key material

jwks.name: jwks-certificate-only
jwks.why: an RSA key given only as a certificate thumbprint: the verifier reads `n` and `e`, not certificates
